faqs.answer: For liquids, ml is more accurate, because jugs are marked in fine steps. For baking, grams on a scale beat both. Cups are best when the recipe was written in cups.

felicityNote: When a recipe is written in milliliters, I reach for the jug, not the cup measure. Converting to cups adds a rounding error at every step, and the jug is already marked.

howToSteps.name: Read the milliliters
howToSteps.text: Find the amount in ml in your recipe. Common amounts are 100, 125, 250, 375, and 500 ml.

howToSteps.name: Divide by 236.588
howToSteps.text: Milliliters divided by 236.588 gives US cups. 250 ml is 1.06 cups, 500 ml is 2.11 cups, 1 liter is 4.23 cups.

howToSteps.name: Round to a fraction you can measure
howToSteps.text: 1.06 cups is a cup and a splash. 0.42 cups is a scant half cup. Round to the nearest quarter cup for cooking, and measure exactly for baking.

howToSteps.name: Check for the metric cup
howToSteps.text: If the recipe also mentions cups, it may mean the metric cup of 250 ml. In that case 250 ml is exactly 1 cup, not 1.06.

lede: 250 ml is just over one US cup. Type milliliters to get cups, or cups to get milliliters, and remember that a metric recipe's cup is 250 ml, not 236.588.

name: Milliliters to Cups
title: Milliliters to US Cups Converter
tutorial: A liter is 4.23 US cups, and a quarter liter is just over a cup. That is the shape of this conversion: metric amounts are usually bigger numbers than the cups they become, because a cup is a small unit next to a liter. 500 ml is 2.11 cups. 250 ml is 1.06 cups. 100 ml is 0.42 cups, which is just under half a cup.

The most common reason to convert this way is a recipe written in milliliters with a cup measure in the drawer. A European recipe that calls for 200 ml of cream is asking for about 0.85 cups, which is just under a cup, or 13 1/2 tablespoons if you want to be exact.

Watch for the metric cup. A recipe written in milliliters may also say cups, and when it does, it usually means the metric cup of 250 ml. A recipe that says 250 ml and 1 cup in the same ingredient list is using the metric cup, and converting 250 ml to US cups gives 1.06, not 1. The difference is small, about 6 percent, but it adds up across a whole cake.

Cup results on this page show two decimals, so 250 ml reads as 1.06 cups. For cooking, round to the nearest sensible fraction: 1.06 cups is a cup and a splash, 0.42 cups is a scant half cup, 2.11 cups is 2 cups and a tablespoon or two.

For baking, the honest answer is to skip cups entirely. A recipe written in milliliters was developed with a jug or a scale, and converting to cups adds error at every step. If the recipe also gives grams, use the scale. If it only gives milliliters, a jug with ml markings is the accurate tool.
